title: Marguerite and the Sigil
premise: When the border wards of Vellamark collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, Lena Amberdale's carefully hidden life as an unlicensed charm-seller shatters: the wards were fed by dragon-fire, and the last dragon is dying beneath Mount Sarn because its heart-flame was sold to the Undercourt. The sigil branded on Lena's palm at her apprenticeship marks her as the only living witch who can walk the court's roads unchallenged, making her both savior and traitor in the eyes of the city that outlawed her craft. Gathering a found family of outcasts—a disgraced warden, a starless astronomer, and a child who remembers magic—she descends to bargain for the soul her old mistress sold to buy Lena's escape fifteen years ago. In the end Lena learns the soul sold was her own shadow-self; she must choose to reclaim it and burn bright, or leave it burning to keep the dragon alive, and she finds a third way by giving the court her sigil instead, extinguishing her invisibility forever but kindling a new fire shared among all who carry it.
about_author: Quentin Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in mountain villages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who survive by staying small, and what happens when smallness finally fails.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A day selling luck-knots and fever-charms in the smuggler's market of Greyharbor, establishing her rules: never big magic, never twice for the same customer, never be remembered. When a customer pays with an old coin stamped with her mistress's sigil, Lena's hands shake. Emotional beat: the loneliness beneath her careful routine.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At midnight every star goes dark and the horizon shudders—the border wards have fallen. Panic floods the city; wardens sweep the streets hunting witches to blame. Lena burns fifteen years of records and flees through rooftops. Emotional beat: terror that the past has finally come collecting.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Knocked
chapters.summary: Dain Corvess's POV. A disgraced border-warden, blamed for the wards' failure, tracks the charm-seller whose sigil matches symbols on the fallen boundary stones. He corners Lena but hesitates when he sees the brand on her palm—his own dead sister bore its twin. Emotional beat: two hunted people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dain reveals the wards weren't built against invaders but fed by dragon-fire from Mount Sarn—and the fire is failing because something was sold below. Lena recognizes the transaction's signature: her mistress Odile's work. Emotional beat: the dawning weight of an inheritance she never wanted.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with flashbacks. Searching Odile's abandoned cottage, Lena finds a ledger showing a payment made fifteen years ago: one soul, sold to the Undercourt, price of passage for 'the girl.' She realizes her escape was bought with someone's soul—possibly her own. Emotional beat: guilt reframing her whole survival as theft.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Counts Stars
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A feral, half-starved child follows Lena through the market ruins, reciting constellations that no longer exist. Wren remembers magic from before the outlawry and refuses to leave. Against every rule, Lena feeds her. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness cracking open a closed heart.

chapters.title: Road Through Ash
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The three flee toward Mount Sarn along the dead border road, pursued by wardens and by hollow-eyed things slipping through the broken wards. Dain teaches them warden signs; Wren names the dark creatures before they name themselves—an old defense. Emotional beat: strangers becoming a unit.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. An old tollhouse offers shelter run by Maren, a hedge-healer who once knew Odile. Maren confirms the soul sold was 'a shadow split from a living girl'—Lena's other half. Lena rages at Odile's ghost. Emotional beat: grief for a mother-figure revealed as a debtor and deceiver.

chapters.title: Hollow Things at the Ford
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the river ford, the hollowed creatures attack, drawn to Lena's sigil. Wren is nearly taken; Lena breaks her own rule and works big magic publicly, burning a hollow thing away with raw will. Wardens see the light. Emotional beat: the cost of survival—her invisibility is spent.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. From a ridge they see Mount Sarn breathing smoke like a dying animal, and far below, doors of green glass opening in the rock. The Undercourt is rising to collect debts now that the wards no longer bind it. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Bargains at the Green Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A herald of the Undercourt offers Lena passage down in exchange for Wren, whose pre-outlawry blood is valuable. Lena refuses; the herald marks her for the Court's hunt instead. Emotional beat: choosing family over safety, knowing the price.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon's Keeper
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. They meet Sorrel, an exiled keeper who tends the dying dragon Vaskarath in the mountain's roots. The dragon's heart-flame gutters because its shadow-half was sold to the Court long ago—mirroring Lena's loss. Emotional beat: recognition that dragon and girl are the same wound.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Running
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, mostly flashback. Around the dragon's fading warmth, Lena tells the full story: Odile splitting her shadow to hide her from the Court, the runaway apprenticeship, the years of small charms and smaller fears. Dain and Wren listen without judgment. Emotional beat: confession as belonging.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Leaving Wren and Sorrel above, Lena and Dain take the keeper's road down through the mountain's glass tunnels toward the Undercourt, guided by the sigil on her palm which glows brighter the deeper they go. Emotional beat: walking willingly into the thing she fled.

chapters.title: The Market of Sold Things
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the Court's bazaar, souls hang like lanterns. Lena finds hers—a flickering grey girl-shape wearing her face—and learns the Court plans to feed it to Vaskarath's flame to keep the mountain burning forever, enslaving the dragon. Emotional beat: horror at being both commodity and key.

chapters.title: Audience with the Pale Regent
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The Regent offers a bargain: Lena may reclaim her soul if she surrenders her sigil and serves the Court as its bound witch, replacing Odile. Lena sees Odile's fate reflected—her mistress chose this once and escaped only by treachery. Emotional beat: temptation of a gilded cage.

chapters.title: The Theft
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. While Lena stalls the Regent, Dain uses warden training to steal the caged shadow-soul from the bazaar, nearly dying to a hollow guard. He escapes wounded, carrying the light. Emotional beat: loyalty proven in blood, the warden breaking his last law.

chapters.title: Reunion of Halves
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Reunited with her shadow, Lena faces the choice: merge and become whole but let the dragon die and the wards stay fallen, or give the shadow to Vaskarath and remain forever halved. Wren arrives uninvited with Sorrel, insisting there's another way. Emotional beat: the impossible arithmetic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Fire Shared Is Fire Multiplied
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Wren's insight: fire hoarded dies, fire shared spreads. Instead of feeding one soul to the dragon, Lena offers her sigil—breaking it apart into embers given to everyone present: dragon, keepers, outcasts, even repentant hollows. The Court's claim shatters; the Regent's power, built on singular debts, collapses. Emotional beat: triumph through generosity rather than conquest.

chapters.title: The Mountain Wakes
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Vaskarath rises, young again on shared flame, and breathes new fire up through the mountain. The stars relight one by one as the wards rebuild themselves woven from many small magics instead of one great secret. The Undercourt retreats, its economy of stolen souls bankrupted. Emotional beat: wonder after long darkness.

chapters.title: Sigils in Every Palm
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Back in Greyharbor, magic is decriminalized; Lena opens a school teaching small charms openly, Wren her first proper student, Dain rebuilding the wards as a covenant rather than a wall. Her palm bears not a brand but a scar shaped like a door. Emotional beat: home built where hiding used to be.

chapters.title: Marguerite and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, years later. Wren, now a teacher herself, tells students the story of Marguerite—the name Odile gave Lena's lost shadow—and how the sigil was broken so no one would ever be sold again. Lena, older, corrects the details fondly. Emotional beat: legacy, and the quiet joy of being known.
